## Setup

```{r}
#| label: Setup_01
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

# Clear all objects from memory
rm(list = ls())

# knitr settings: ensures code is echoed and figures are centered
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, fig.align = "center")
options(tinytex.verbose = TRUE)

# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(100)

# Define paths to the different data files and function scripts

paths <- list(
  DESIGN = "Input/01_dadapipe/01_design/design.xlsx",
  bcount = "Input/01_dadapipe/13_output/bacteria/100/bacteria_COUNT100.tab",
  btaxa = "Input/01_dadapipe/13_output/bacteria/100/bacteria_TAXA100.tab",
  bseq = "Input/01_dadapipe/13_output/bacteria/100/bacteria_SEQ100.fasta",
  fcount = "Input/01_dadapipe/13_output/fungi/100/fungi_COUNT100.tab",
  ftaxa = "Input/01_dadapipe/13_output/fungi/100/fungi_TAXA100.tab",
  otaxa = "Input/02_blast/oomycetes_TAXA100_NCBI.tab",
  fseq = "Input/01_dadapipe/13_output/fungi/100/fungi_SEQ100.fasta",
  fprimers = "Input/03_primer_tracing/03_R/fOTU_primer.RDS",
  host_amplicon = "Input/At.GI_amplicon.fasta",
  functions = "Input/functions/"
)

# Set source file location for running code interactively (for rendering it's set in the YAML)
if (interactive()) {
if (!require(rstudioapi)) { install.packages("rstudioapi") }
library(rstudioapi)
setwd(dirname(getActiveDocumentContext()$path))
}

#set CRAN mirror for downloading libraries
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://stat.ethz.ch/CRAN/")) #ETH Switzerland

# Load custom functions from the specified path
source(paste0(paths$functions, "functions.R"))
functions(path = paths$functions)

# Install (if necessary) and load required libraries
libraries()
library("knitr")

```

## Load and prepare DESIGN objects

We import the metadata of each sample.

```{r}
#| label: design objects
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false


#import design file
DESIGN <- read_excel(paths$DESIGN, sheet = "Sheet1")

#line

DESIGN$line <- factor(DESIGN$line, levels=c("WT","318"))
DESIGN <- DESIGN[!(is.na(DESIGN$line)),]

# Assign custom colors to lines for visualization purposes
DESIGN$cols_line <- NA
DESIGN$cols_line[DESIGN$line == "WT"] <- "#01686c"
DESIGN$cols_line[DESIGN$line == "318"] <- "#e3913e"

# Create a collapsed color vector for the lines
temp <- data.frame(DESIGN$line, DESIGN$cols_line)  #collaps color vector
temp <- plyr::ddply(temp, .variables="DESIGN.cols_line", .fun=unique)
level_cols_line <- as.character(temp[,2])
names(level_cols_line) <- temp[,1]
rm(temp)

# Assign colors based on experimental conditions (plus/minus)
DESIGN$cols_condition <- NA
DESIGN$cols_condition[DESIGN$condition == "minus"] <- "seagreen"
DESIGN$cols_condition[DESIGN$condition == "plus"] <- "gold2"

# Collapse condition color vectors similarly
temp <- data.frame(DESIGN$condition, DESIGN$cols_condition)
temp <- plyr::ddply(temp, .variables="DESIGN.cols_condition", .fun=unique)
level_cols_condition <- as.character(temp[,2])
names(level_cols_condition) <- temp[,1]


#remove unscaled samples
DESIGN <- DESIGN[!(grepl("unscaled",DESIGN$sub_libr, fixed=T)),]

#remove At duplicates
DESIGN <- DESIGN[!(grepl("dupl_for_At", DESIGN$sub_libr, fixed=T)),]

#add oomaycetes and arabidopsis taxa (not done before because of the dadapipe)
DESIGN$taxa[DESIGN$sub_libr=="oomycetes"] <- "oomycetes"

#separate DESIGN file
bDESIGN <- DESIGN[DESIGN$taxa=="bacteria",]
fDESIGN <- DESIGN[DESIGN$taxa=="fungi",]
oDESIGN <- DESIGN[DESIGN$taxa=="oomycetes",]

#overwrite sample nbr (if in same order)
if(sum(bDESIGN$sample_nr == fDESIGN$sample_nr)==nrow(bDESIGN) &
   sum(bDESIGN$sample_nr == oDESIGN$sample_nr)==nrow(bDESIGN)){
  bDESIGN$sample_nr <- paste0("sample", 1:nrow(bDESIGN))
  fDESIGN$sample_nr <- paste0("sample", 1:nrow(fDESIGN))
  oDESIGN$sample_nr <- paste0("sample", 1:nrow(oDESIGN))

}

```

## Load and prepare COUNT objects

We import the raw COUNT tables and subset them to only contain samples used in this analysis as \_COUNTa (all ASVs). We then subset the ASVs to only contain those where reads are present in at least 1 sample.

```{r}
#| label: bCOUNT objects
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

#bacteria

#import ASV table
bCOUNTa <- read.delim(paths$bcount, header=T, row.names=1, sep="\t")
bCOUNTa <- t(bCOUNTa)

# adapt names
colnames(bCOUNTa) <- gsub("BS09_", "", colnames(bCOUNTa))
rownames(bCOUNTa) <- gsub("OTU", "bASV", rownames(bCOUNTa))

#sort (and remove unused samples)
order <- match(bDESIGN$bc_ID, colnames(bCOUNTa))
bCOUNTa <- as.data.frame(bCOUNTa[, order])
rm(order)

#remove OTU with 0 seqs (not present in selected samples)
bCOUNTa <- bCOUNTa[rowSums(bCOUNTa) >0,]


```

## Load and prepare TAXA objects

We load the TAXA tables, subset them to samples contain only microbial and host ASVs and match ASVs present in the COUNT tables

```{r}
#| label: Load and filter bTAXA
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
#| paged-print: false
# --- Load and filter bTAXA ---
#BACTERIA

#import taxonomy table
bTAXA <- read.table(paths$btaxa, row.names=1, sep="\t", blank.lines.skip = FALSE)

#rename
colnames(bTAXA) <- tolower(colnames(bTAXA))
bTAXA[is.na(bTAXA)] <- "unassigned"
rownames(bTAXA) <- gsub("OTU", "bASV", rownames(bTAXA))

#remove OTU with 0 seqs
bTAXA <- bTAXA[rownames(bTAXA) %in% rownames(bCOUNTa),]

# define ASVs for removal
r2 <- -which(bTAXA$phylum=="Cyanobacteria")
r3 <- -which(bTAXA$family=="Mitochondria")
r4 <- -which(is.na(bTAXA)) #rows all na
ASVs_to_remove <- c(r2,r3,r4)
if(length(ASVs_to_remove)>0){
  bTAXA <- bTAXA[ASVs_to_remove ,]
  bCOUNTm <- bCOUNTa[rownames(bTAXA),]
}
rm(r2,r3,r4,ASVs_to_remove)

#add ASV_ID
bTAXA$ASV_ID <- rownames(bTAXA)
#levels
bTAXA$phylum <- as.factor(bTAXA$phylum)
# defining ASV colors by phylum (using the bTAXAonomy file)
bTAXA$labels <- as.character(bTAXA$phylum)
bTAXA$labels[bTAXA$kingdom == "Eukaryota"] <- "Host"

# create separate bTAXAonomy label specifying classes of Proteobacteria
bTAXA$class <- as.factor(bTAXA$class)
try(bTAXA[ bTAXA$class=="Alphaproteobacteria", ]$labels <- "Alphaproteobacteria")
try(bTAXA[ bTAXA$class=="Betaproteobacteria", ]$labels <- "Betaproteobacteria")
try(bTAXA[ bTAXA$class=="Gammaproteobacteria", ]$labels <- "Gammaproteobacteria")
try(bTAXA[ bTAXA$class=="Deltaproteobacteria", ]$labels <- "Deltaproteobacteria")
bTAXA$labels <- as.factor(bTAXA$labels)

```

```{r}
fTAXA$labels[rownames(fTAXA) %in% Host_ASVs] <- "Host"

#use NCBI to get At classification
#fTAXA$labels[rownames(fTAXA)==paste0("f",Host_ASVs)] <- "Host"

Host_taxonomy <- read.delim(paths$otaxa) %>% filter(genus == "Arabidopsis")
fTAXA[fTAXA$labels=="Host",1:8] <- Host_taxonomy

#factor
fTAXA$phylum <- as.factor(fTAXA$phylum)
fTAXA$labels <- as.factor(fTAXA$labels)
```

## Define host sequences

We compare the eukaryotic ASVs to the At.GI sequence and remove eukaryotic ASVs which are less similar than 99%. We rename the sequences matching to GIGANEA as Host (to be used later in 02_Taxa_Analysis.qmd).

### Bacteria

```{r}
#| label: host amplicon bac
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

# BACTERIA

#At-gigantea seq
AtSEQ <- Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(paths$host_amplicon)
AtSEQ <- as.data.frame(AtSEQ)
colnames(AtSEQ) <- "seqs"

#host seqs
bSEQ <- Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(paths$bseq)
bSEQ <- as.data.frame(bSEQ)
colnames(bSEQ) <- "seqs"
rownames(bSEQ) <- gsub("OTU", "bASV", rownames(bSEQ))
eOTU <- rownames(bTAXA)[bTAXA$labels=="Host"] #eukaryotic OTUs
eSEQ <- bSEQ[rownames(bSEQ) %in% eOTU,, drop=F] #eukaryotic seqs
rm(bSEQ, eOTU)

### MAPPING ###

#create new data.frame to save distances
distances <- data.frame(matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(AtSEQ), ncol = nrow(eSEQ)), row.names = rownames(AtSEQ))
colnames(distances) <- rownames(eSEQ)

#mapping function
map <- function(AtSEQ) {
  eSEQs_to_map <- data.frame(seqs=c(as.character(AtSEQ),as.character(eSEQ$seqs[i]))) #create data.frame with hSEQ and bSEQ to map
  eSEQs_to_map <- Biostrings::DNAStringSet(eSEQs_to_map$seqs) #convert to DNA string set
  eSEQs_aln <- DECIPHER::AlignSeqs(eSEQs_to_map, processors = 1, verbose = F) #align, processors = NULL uses the max available number of processors
  dist_all <- DECIPHER::DistanceMatrix(eSEQs_aln, processors = 1, verbose = F) #similarity table
  return(dist_all[1,2])
}

#calculate distances
for(i in 1:nrow(eSEQ)) {distances[,i] <- apply(AtSEQ, 1, map)}

#similarity
similarities <- 1 - distances

#add OTU abundance and plot
similarities <- rbind(similarities, n_seqs=rowSums(bCOUNTm[rownames(bCOUNTm)%in%colnames(distances),]))
pander(t(similarities))


#remove ASVs
ASVs_to_remove <- colnames(similarities)[similarities[1,]<0.99]
bCOUNTm <- bCOUNTm[!(rownames(bCOUNTm) %in% ASVs_to_remove),]
bTAXA <- bTAXA[!(rownames(bTAXA) %in% ASVs_to_remove),]
zeroASVs_to_remove <- names(which(colSums(bCOUNTm) == 0))
bCOUNTm <- bCOUNTm[,!(colnames(bCOUNTm) %in% zeroASVs_to_remove)]
bTAXA <- bTAXA[!(rownames(bTAXA) %in% zeroASVs_to_remove),]

if(length(ASVs_to_remove)>0){
  print(paste0("The following eukaryotic ASVs were removed: ", paste(ASVs_to_remove, collapse = ", ")))
} else{
  print("No eukaryotic ASVs were removed")
}

rm(eSEQ, AtSEQ, similarities, ASVs_to_remove, zeroASVs_to_remove, distances)

```

### Fungi

```{r}

#| echo: false

  eSEQs_to_map <- Biostrings::DNAStringSet(eSEQs_to_map$seqs) #convert to DNA string set
  eSEQs_aln <- DECIPHER::AlignSeqs(eSEQs_to_map, processors = 1, verbose = F) #align, processors = NULL uses the max available number of processors
  dist_all <- DECIPHER::DistanceMatrix(eSEQs_aln, processors = 1, verbose = F) #similarity table
  return(dist_all[1,2])
}

#calculate distances
for(i in 1:nrow(eSEQ)) {distances[,i] <- apply(AtSEQ, 1, map)}

#similarity
similarities <- 1 - distances

#add ASV abundance and plot
similarities <- rbind(similarities, n_seqs=rowSums(fCOUNTm[rownames(fCOUNTm)%in%colnames(distances),]))
pander(t(similarities))

#remove ASVs
ASVs_to_remove <- colnames(similarities)[similarities[1,]<0.99]
fCOUNTm <- fCOUNTm[!(rownames(fCOUNTm) %in% ASVs_to_remove),]
fTAXA <- fTAXA[!(rownames(fTAXA) %in% ASVs_to_remove),]
zeroASVs_to_remove <- names(which(colSums(fCOUNTm) == 0))
fCOUNTm <- fCOUNTm[,!(colnames(fCOUNTm) %in% zeroASVs_to_remove)]
fTAXA <- fTAXA[!(rownames(fTAXA) %in% zeroASVs_to_remove),]

if(length(ASVs_to_remove)>0){
  print(paste0("The following eukaryotic ASVs were removed: ", paste(ASVs_to_remove, collapse = ", ")))
} else{
  print("No eukaryotic ASVs were removed")
}

rm(eSEQ, AtSEQ, similarities, ASVs_to_remove, zeroASVs_to_remove, distances)

```

## Sequencing depth

### Sequencing depth - plots

```{r}
#| label: Sequencing depth - plots
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false
#Bacateria

#boxplot
df <- data.frame(col_sum=colSums(bCOUNTm),colnames=colnames(bCOUNTm), line=bDESIGN$line, condition=bDESIGN$condition)
ylim2=max(colSums(bCOUNTm))
bac_seq_nr <- seq_nr_plot(df, "Bacteria: Sequencing depth") #create plot

## barplot
df <- df[order(df$col_sum, decreasing = T),]
df <- df[order(df$condition),]
df$x <- c(1:sum(df$condition == "minus"), 1:sum(df$condition == "plus"))
bac_samples <- samples_plot(df) #create plot

#Fungi

#boxplot
df <- data.frame(col_sum=colSums(fCOUNTm),colnames=colnames(fCOUNTm), line=fDESIGN$line, condition=fDESIGN$condition)
ylim2=max(colSums(fCOUNTm))
fun_seq_nr <- seq_nr_plot(df, "Fungi: Sequencing depth") #create plot

## barplot
df <- df[order(df$col_sum, decreasing = T),]
df <- df[order(df$condition),]
df$x <- c(1:sum(df$condition == "minus"), 1:sum(df$condition == "plus"))
fun_samples <- samples_plot(df) #create plot

#Oomycetes

#boxplot
df <- data.frame(col_sum=colSums(oCOUNTm),colnames=colnames(oCOUNTm), line=oDESIGN$line, condition=oDESIGN$condition)
ylim2=max(colSums(oCOUNTm))
oom_seq_nr <- seq_nr_plot(df, "Oomycetes: Sequencing depth") #create plot

## barplot
df <- df[order(df$col_sum, decreasing = T),]
df <- df[order(df$condition),]
df$x <- c(1:sum(df$condition == "minus"), 1:sum(df$condition == "plus"))
oom_samples <- samples_plot(df) #create plot



#combine the plots (library cowplot)
plot <- plot_grid(bac_seq_nr + theme(legend.position="none"),
               fun_seq_nr + theme(legend.position="none") + labs(colour=""),
               oom_seq_nr + theme(legend.position="none") + labs(colour=""),
               bac_samples + theme(legend.position="none") + labs(colour=""),
               fun_samples + theme(legend.position="none") + labs(colour=""),
               oom_samples + theme(legend.position="none") + labs(colour=""),
               #labels=c("A","B"),
               align = "hv",
               rel_heights = c(9,5),
               nrow=2)

legend <- get_legend(bac_seq_nr + theme(legend.position="bottom") + labs(fill="line"))
```

\pagebreak

## Normalization

### Asymptotic Kruskal-Wallis test

We test for different sequencing depths between the treatments

#### Bacteria

```{r}
#| label: sequencing depths bact
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

# Bacteria
group <- paste(bDESIGN$line, bDESIGN$condition, sep="_") %>% as.factor
sample_depth <- colSums(bCOUNTm)
DAT_krusk <- coin::kruskal_test(sample_depth ~ group)
DAT_krusk

#get rarefaction threshold (round down to 100)
brare_threshold <- floor((min(sample_depth))/100)*100

rm(group, sample_depth, DAT_krusk)

```

#### Fungi

```{r}
#| label: seq numbers per group fun
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

# Bacteria
group <- paste(fDESIGN$line, fDESIGN$condition, sep="_") %>% as.factor
sample_depth <- colSums(fCOUNTm)
DAT_krusk <- coin::kruskal_test(sample_depth ~ group)
DAT_krusk

#get rarefaction threshold (round down to 100)
frare_threshold <- floor((min(sample_depth))/100)*100

rm(group, sample_depth, DAT_krusk)

```

#### Oomycetes

```{r}
#| label: seq numbers per group oom
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

# Bacteria
group <- paste(oDESIGN$line, oDESIGN$condition, sep="_") %>% as.factor
sample_depth <- colSums(oCOUNTm)
DAT_krusk <- coin::kruskal_test(sample_depth ~ group)
DAT_krusk

#get rarefaction threshold (round down to 100)
orare_threshold <- floor((min(sample_depth))/100)*100

rm(group, sample_depth, DAT_krusk)

```

**Conclusion:** Because there are significant differences between the treatments in bacteria and oomycetes, we normalize the data by rarefication for diversity comparisions (see Weiss et al. (2017), Microbiome Journal). For consistency we do it for bacteria, fungi and oomycetes. We define the rarefaction threshold per sample to `r brare_threshold` for bacteria, `r frare_threshold` for fungi and `r orare_threshold` for oomycetes.

## Sample control

### Outlier detection

We use the method CLOUD developped by Montassier et al. 2018, which is a non.parametric detection test for outliers. We perform the test with Bray-Curtis distances from the rarefied data for each substrate and each plastic treatment individually. We set the number of nearest neighbors to 60% of the samples size and chose an empirical outlier percentile of 0.1. We remove all outliers from our data.

```{r}
#| label: outlier detection
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

#function to detect outliers
detect_outliers <- function(DESIGN, COUNT_norm, line){

  #subset
  samples_sub <- DESIGN$sample_name[DESIGN$line %in% line]
  DAT_sub <- COUNT_norm[,colnames(COUNT_norm) %in% samples_sub]
  bdist <- vegdist(t(DAT_sub), method="bray")

  #test
  k <- floor(ncol(DAT_sub) * 0.6) #number of nearest neighbors, here we chose 60% of sample size
  test <- piecewise_kn_V1(d = bdist, test.ix = colnames(DAT_sub), k = k) #CLOUD test from Montassier et al. 2018
  outliers <- colnames(DAT_sub)[test[["pvals"]]<=0.1] #outliers (p <= 0.1)

  return(outliers)

}

#detect outliers
boutliers <- detect_outliers(DESIGN=bDESIGN, COUNT_norm=bCOUNTm_norm, line=unique(bDESIGN$line))
foutliers <- detect_outliers(DESIGN=fDESIGN, COUNT_norm=fCOUNTm_norm, line=unique(fDESIGN$line))
ooutliers <- detect_outliers(DESIGN=oDESIGN, COUNT_norm=oCOUNTm_norm, line=unique(oDESIGN$line))

#output
outliers <- data.frame(taxa=c("Bacteria","Fungi","Oomycetes"),
                       outliers=c(length(boutliers), length(foutliers), length(ooutliers)))


pander(outliers, caption = "Number of outliers")

print(paste("Bacteria:", paste(boutliers, collapse = ", ")))
print(paste("Fungi:", paste(foutliers, collapse = ", ")))
print(paste("Oomycetes:", paste(ooutliers, collapse = ", ")))

```

### Outlier removal

```{r}
#| label: outlier removal
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| paged-print: false

#Bacteria
bDESIGN <- bDESIGN[!(bDESIGN$sample_name %in% boutliers),]
bCOUNTm_norm <- bCOUNTm_norm[,!(colnames(bCOUNTm_norm) %in% boutliers)]
ASVs_to_remove <- names(which(rowSums(bCOUNTm_norm) == 0))
bCOUNTm_norm <- bCOUNTm_norm[!(rownames(bCOUNTm_norm) %in% ASVs_to_remove),]
bTAXA_norm <- bTAXA_norm[!(rownames(bTAXA_norm) %in% ASVs_to_remove),]
# Remove outlier samples first;To be used later for diff abundance
bCOUNTm <- bCOUNTm[, !(colnames(bCOUNTm) %in% boutliers)] 
# Keep only ASVs present in the normalized (rarefied) table
bCOUNTm <- bCOUNTm[rownames(bCOUNTm) %in% rownames(bCOUNTm_norm), ]

#Fungi
fDESIGN <- fDESIGN[!(fDESIGN$sample_name %in% foutliers),]
fCOUNTm_norm <- fCOUNTm_norm[,!(colnames(fCOUNTm_norm) %in% foutliers)]
ASVs_to_remove <- names(which(rowSums(fCOUNTm_norm) == 0))
fCOUNTm_norm <- fCOUNTm_norm[!(rownames(fCOUNTm_norm) %in% ASVs_to_remove),]
fTAXA_norm <- fTAXA_norm[!(rownames(fTAXA_norm) %in% ASVs_to_remove),]
# Remove outlier samples first;To be used later for diff abundance
fCOUNTm <- fCOUNTm[, !(colnames(fCOUNTm) %in% foutliers)] 
# Keep only ASVs present in the normalized (rarefied) table
fCOUNTm <- fCOUNTm[rownames(fCOUNTm) %in% rownames(fCOUNTm_norm), ]

#Oomycetes
oDESIGN <- oDESIGN[!(oDESIGN$sample_name %in% ooutliers),]
oCOUNTm_norm <- oCOUNTm_norm[,!(colnames(oCOUNTm_norm) %in% ooutliers)]
ASVs_to_remove <- names(which(rowSums(oCOUNTm_norm) == 0))
oCOUNTm_norm <- oCOUNTm_norm[!(rownames(oCOUNTm_norm) %in% ASVs_to_remove),]
oTAXA_norm <- oTAXA_norm[!(rownames(oTAXA_norm) %in% ASVs_to_remove),]
# Remove outlier samples first;To be used later for diff abundance
oCOUNTm <- oCOUNTm[, !(colnames(oCOUNTm) %in% ooutliers)] 
# Keep only ASVs present in the normalized (rarefied) table
oCOUNTm <- oCOUNTm[rownames(oCOUNTm) %in% rownames(oCOUNTm_norm), ]

```
